subQuestions.questionText:
The hormone that prepares the body for an emergency is …
A aldosterone.
B progesterone.
C adrenalin.
D prolactin.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Adrenalin (adrenaline) is released by the adrenal medulla and prepares the body for an emergency (the 'fight-or-flight' response).

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following are functions of the placenta?
A Excretion and nutrition
B Gaseous exchange and protection against mechanical injury
C Nutrition and temperature regulation
D Temperature regulation and excretion
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The placenta carries out excretion (removal of embryonic wastes) and nutrition (supply of nutrients). Protection against mechanical injury is a function of the amniotic fluid, and the placenta does not regulate temperature.

options.B: Gaseous exchange and protection against mechanical injury

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the reaction time of four learners to a stimulus.
NAME OF LEARNER | REACTION TIME (SECONDS)
Temisha | 0,7
Luke | 0,6
Anika | 0,8
Jordy | 0,4
Which ONE of the following learners demonstrates the fastest response to the stimulus?
A Temisha
B Luke
C Anika
D Jordy
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Jordy has the shortest reaction time (0,4 seconds), which means the fastest response to the stimulus.

subQuestions.questionText:
A high level of thyroxin in the blood will stimulate the …
A pituitary gland to secrete less TSH.
B thyroid gland to secrete more TSH.
C pituitary gland to secrete more TSH.
D thyroid gland to secrete more thyroxin.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
By negative feedback, a high level of thyroxin inhibits the pituitary gland so that it secretes less TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone).

options.A: pituitary gland to secrete less TSH.
options.B: thyroid gland to secrete more TSH.
options.C: pituitary gland to secrete more TSH.
options.D: thyroid gland to secrete more thyroxin.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following combinations is CORRECT for a normal pregnancy?
  SITE OF FERTILISATION | SITE OF IMPLANTATION
A P | S
B S | Q
C P | Q
D R | P
(Refer to the diagram of the female reproductive system in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
In a normal pregnancy fertilisation takes place in the Fallopian tube (P) and implantation occurs in the uterus (Q).

subQuestions.questionText:
In which part does the zygote develop into a morula?
A S
B Q
C R
D P
(Refer to the diagram of the female reproductive system in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
The zygote develops into a morula in the Fallopian tube (P) as it moves towards the uterus.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following is a list of male reproductive parts:
(i) Prostate gland
(ii) Seminal vesicle
(iii) Urethra
(iv) Cowper's gland
Which ONE of the following combinations is responsible for the formation of semen?
A (i) and (ii) only
B (i), (ii) and (iv) only
C (ii) and (iii) only
D (i) and (iv) only
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Semen is formed by the secretions of the prostate gland (i), the seminal vesicle (ii) and Cowper's (bulbo-urethral) gland (iv). The urethra only transports semen; it does not form it.

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram below represents a human sperm. This sperm is NOT structurally suitable for fertilisation because of the …
A absence of a nucleus to provide genetic material.
B absence of an acrosome to improve motility.
C presence of a long tail for the movement of the sperm.
D absence of mitochondria to provide energy.
(Refer to the sperm diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Without mitochondria the sperm cannot produce the energy (ATP) needed to swim to and fertilise the ovum, so it is not structurally suitable for fertilisation.

options.A: absence of a nucleus to provide genetic material.
options.B: absence of an acrosome to improve motility.
options.C: presence of a long tail for the movement of the sperm.
options.D: absence of mitochondria to provide energy.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following is a list of growth responses in plants:
(i) Plants grow straight upwards
(ii) No upward growth
(iii) Increased number of lateral branches
(iv) Stems bend towards unilateral light
Which ONE of the following combinations describes the growth responses that occur when apical buds of plants are removed?
A (i), (ii) and (iii) only
B (ii) and (iii) only
C (i) and (iv) only
D (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Removing the apical bud removes apical dominance, so there is no further upward growth (ii) and an increased number of lateral branches develop (iii).

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is CORRECT for a person who exercises on a hot day without taking in any liquids?
A Increased ADH secretion and increased permeability of renal tubules
B Increased ADH secretion and the production of dilute urine
C Decreased ADH secretion and increased permeability of renal tubules
D Decreased ADH secretion and the production of concentrated urine
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Exercising on a hot day without drinking causes dehydration (low blood water). This triggers increased ADH secretion, which increases the permeability of the renal tubules so more water is reabsorbed and concentrated urine is produced.

options.A: Increased ADH secretion and increased permeability of renal tubules
options.B: Increased ADH secretion and the production of dilute urine
options.C: Decreased ADH secretion and increased permeability of renal tubules
options.D: Decreased ADH secretion and the production of concentrated urine

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The release of an ovum from the ovary.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The extra-embryonic membrane that plays a role in the formation of the placenta.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: A plant hormone responsible for seed dormancy.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The maintenance of a constant internal environment within narrow limits.
subQuestions.memoText: Homeostasis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description in COLUMN I applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items in COLUMN II.
Description: The hormone responsible for the development of secondary sexual characteristics during puberty.
A: Oestrogen
B: Testosterone
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B (2 marks)
Oestrogen brings about female secondary sexual characteristics and testosterone brings about male secondary sexual characteristics during puberty.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description in COLUMN I applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items in COLUMN II.
Description: Plays a role in the pupillary mechanism.
A: Ciliary muscles
B: Radial muscles
subQuestions.memoText:
B only (2 marks)
The radial muscles of the iris control the size of the pupil (the pupillary mechanism). The ciliary muscles control the shape of the lens (accommodation), not the pupil.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description in COLUMN I applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items in COLUMN II.
Description: A plant defence mechanism.
A: Thorns
B: Chemicals
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B (2 marks)
Both thorns (a physical/structural defence) and chemicals (a chemical defence) are plant defence mechanisms against herbivores.

subQuestions.questionText:
In bird eggs, the yolk is the main source of energy for the developing embryo. The table below provides information about the eggs of some bird types.
TYPE OF BIRD | AVERAGE % OF YOLK IN THE EGG
Goose | 35,1
Eagle | 12,0
Duck | 35,4
Vulture | 14,0
Chicken | 31,9
Pigeon | 17,9
Explain why we may conclude that ducks display precocial development.
subQuestions.memoText:
Compulsory mark (*) plus any 2 (3 marks):
• The egg has a high percentage (%) of yolk* (compulsory) therefore it
• contains more energy / nutrients
• The hatchling will be well developed making it
• (more) independent

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the table of bird types and average % of yolk in the egg. Name the THREE bird types that would have a higher degree of parental care.
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks). Mark first THREE only:
• Eagle
• Vulture
• Pigeon

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 2.1.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
• The eggs have a lower percentage (%) of yolk therefore
• the hatchlings will not be fully developed

The diagram shows a part of the male reproductive system (parts A, B labelled Scrotum, and C). Give the LETTER and the NAME of the:
(a) Gland that secretes testosterone
(b) Part that stores sperm until maturation
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) C – Testis (2 marks: 1 for letter, 1 for name)
(b) A – Epididymis (2 marks: 1 for letter, 1 for name)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the role of the scrotum in sperm production.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following pairs (2 marks):
Option 1: It maintains the temperature of the testes / part C lower than body temperature (1) to ensure the production of good quality / quantity of sperm (1)
Option 2: It protects the testes from (mechanical) injury (1) to ensure the production of good quality / quantity of sperm (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Name and describe the process of sperm production.
subQuestions.memoText:
Compulsory mark (*) plus any 4 (5 marks):
• Spermatogenesis* (compulsory)
• Under the influence of testosterone
• diploid cells
• in the seminiferous tubules / testes
• undergo meiosis
• to form haploid (sperm) cells

subQuestions.questionText:
The thickness of the endometrium varies throughout the menstrual cycle. The table below shows the endometrial thickness recorded for a woman over one menstrual cycle.
DAY OF THE MENSTRUAL CYCLE | THICKNESS OF THE ENDOMETRIUM (mm)
0 | 14
7 | 3
14 | 5
21 | 13
28 | 16
Referring to ovarian hormones, explain the:
(a) Decrease in thickness of the endometrium from day 0 to day 7
(b) Increase in thickness of the endometrium from day 7 to day 14
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) (3 marks):
• The corpus luteum degenerates therefore
• the progesterone levels decrease
• The endometrium is no longer maintained / menstruation occurs
(b) (2 marks):
• the Graafian follicle secretes
• oestrogen which increases endometrium thickness

subQuestions.questionText: Describe changes in the endometrium that cause it to become thicker.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
• It becomes more vascular and
• more glandular

subQuestions.questionText: State the significance of the change in endometrium thickness described in QUESTION 2.3.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• It allows for implantation of the embryo / the development of the placenta / increased blood supply for nutrition of the developing embryo

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a bar graph to show the results in the table (Day of the menstrual cycle vs Thickness of the endometrium in mm).
subQuestions.memoText:
Criteria for marking the graph (6 marks):
• Type of graph: Bar graph is drawn (T) – 1
• Caption of the graph includes both variables (C) – 1
• Correct labels for X-axis and Y-axis and correct unit for Y-axis (L) – 1
• Equal space and width of bars for X-axis and correct scale for Y-axis (S) – 1
• Plotting (P): 1–4 co-ordinates plotted correctly – 1; all 5 co-ordinates plotted correctly – 2
Caption example: 'Thickness of the endometrium for (different) days of the menstrual cycle'. Data to plot: (0, 14), (7, 3), (14, 5), (21, 13), (28, 16).
If a histogram or line graph is drawn, marks are lost for Type of graph and Scale. If axes are transposed: can get all marks if labels are also swopped and bars are horizontal; if labels do not correspond, marks lost for labels and scale, but plotting can get credit if coordinates are correct for the given labels.

subQuestions.questionText: The diagrams (X, Y and Z) represent differences in the diameter of an arteriole close to the surface of the skin during thermoregulation. Diagram Y shows the arteriole under normal conditions. Name the part of the brain that controls thermoregulation.
subQuestions.memoText: Hypothalamus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give the LETTER of the diagram which represents the arteriole on a cold day.
(Refer to diagrams X, Y and Z in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: (Diagram) X (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Explain the significance of the change in the diameter of the arteriole from normal conditions to the condition in diagram Z.
(Refer to diagrams Y and Z in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(4 marks)
• The arteriole dilates / vasodilation took place
• More blood flows to the (surface of) the skin and
• more heat is lost / more radiation occurs to
• decrease / regulate the body temperature

subQuestions.questionText:
Idiopathic Short Stature (ISS) describes a condition where children have normal birth height, but grow slowly and do not reach the expected height for their age group (NOT due to malnutrition or lifestyle). Scientists investigated the effect of added growth hormone on the height of children with ISS. Procedure: consent was obtained from parents of a group of two-year-old boys with ISS; the boys were divided into two groups; Group A received human growth hormone at a daily dosage of 0,028 mg per kg of body weight; Group B did not receive the hormone treatment; the height of participants was measured monthly until each reached 18 years of age. At 18 years, the average height in Group A was 8 cm more than that in Group B.
State the dependent variable of this investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: Height (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: List THREE variables that were kept constant and which contributed to the validity of the investigation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE (3 marks). Mark first THREE only:
• Gender / only boys participated
• All (the boys) had ISS
• Age / all (the boys) were 2 years old
• Duration of investigation

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the purpose of Group B in this investigation.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
To prove that it is the added growth hormone that caused the change in the height of the boys and not any other factor.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the daily amount of added human growth hormone that was given to a boy with a mass of 25 kg. Show ALL your working, INCLUDING the correct unit.
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks)
Working: (25 × 0,028)
Answer: = 0,7 mg

subQuestions.questionText: Give a conclusion for this investigation.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
Added growth hormone causes an increase in height of children with ISS.

Describe the pathway of an impulse from part D through the spinal cord to part E, to bring about a reflex action.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 6 (6 marks):
• (The impulse) is transmitted by the sensory neuron
• via the dorsal root of the spinal nerve to
• the interneuron and to
• the motor neuron
• by synaptic contact
• It is then transmitted via the ventral root (of the spinal nerve)
• to the effector which brings about the reflex action

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how the human eye ACCOMMODATES for distant vision.
subQuestions.memoText:
(5 marks)
• Ciliary muscles relax
• Suspensory ligaments become taut / tension on the lens increases
• The lens becomes less convex causing
• light to be refracted less
• to form a clear image on the retina

Give the LETTERS of TWO parts that are normally filled with fluid.

subQuestions.memoText: C and D (2 marks). Mark first TWO only.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how balance is restored when there is a change in the speed and direction of head movement.
subQuestions.memoText:
(5 marks)
• Cristae are stimulated and
• convert the stimulus to an impulse which
• is sent via the auditory nerve
• to the cerebellum for interpretation
• Impulses are then sent to the skeletal muscles to restore balance

subQuestions.questionText:
When a person is exposed to loud noise over a long period, it may lead to noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL), which is caused by damage to the hair cells in the organ of Corti. These cells are not repaired when damaged. Placing earplugs in the auditory canal can prevent damage to the hair cells. Explain how:
(a) Damage to the hair cells in the organ of Corti can lead to hearing loss
(b) Earplugs can prevent damage to the hair cells in the organ of Corti
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) (2 marks):
• Fewer / no stimuli will be converted into impulses
• Fewer / no impulses will be sent to the cerebrum to be interpreted
(b) (3 marks):
• The earplugs limit the sound waves in the auditory canal / reaching the tympanic membrane
• Fewer vibrations are formed in the middle ear
• Fewer pressure waves are formed in the cochlea to prevent damage

subQuestions.questionText:
The graph shows the insulin levels of three people over a 23-hour period:
Person A: A healthy person who received no treatment.
Person B: A person with diabetes mellitus who received a rapid-acting insulin injection before each meal.
Person C: A person with diabetes mellitus who received a daily injection containing long-acting insulin at 23:00.
All three people received the same meals at the same time of the day.
Name the organ that secretes insulin.
subQuestions.memoText: Pancreas (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
State the number of meals that were eaten during the 23-hour period.
(Refer to the graph in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Three / nine (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Tabulate TWO differences between long-acting insulin treatment and rapid-acting insulin treatment over the 23-hour period.
(Refer to the graph in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Table (1) plus any (2 × 2) differences (5 marks). Mark first TWO only. Any TWO of the following paired differences:
LONG-ACTING INSULIN TREATMENT vs RAPID-ACTING INSULIN TREATMENT:
• One injection is given over 23 hours | Three injections are given over 23 hours
• The injection is given at 23:00 | An injection is given before every meal
• The injection causes a lower concentration of insulin / 10 international units | The injection causes a higher concentration of insulin / 30 international units
• The concentration of insulin in the blood remains constant for long periods of time / 20 hours | The concentration of insulin in the blood fluctuates / increases and drops
• Long lasting effect | Lasts a shorter amount of time
• Insulin concentration takes 1 hour to increase to its peak | Insulin concentration takes 2 hours to increase to its peak

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the type of insulin treatment that is similar to insulin secretion in a healthy person.
(Refer to the graph in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Rapid-acting insulin (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why person B may experience a lack of energy after receiving a rapid-acting insulin injection if NO meal is taken.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
• The insulin will reduce the glucose level even further / glucose is converted to glycogen / increased glucose uptake by cells
• There is less glucose available for cellular respiration
